title: Etwas ist schiefgegangen
subtitle: Telling a story in writing, with the right past in the right place
words.intro: Every summer castle courtyards fill with people in chain mail. They are accountants and dentists from Monday to Friday. The rest of the week, they’d like you to call them Sir.
words.more: Auch auf der Burg · also at the castle

grammar[0].blocks[1].title: Words for the practice page
grammar[0].fact: German schoolchildren write a *Bildergeschichte* and an *Erlebnisaufsatz*, a story of something that happened, and learn the signal words at about nine: *plötzlich* is the word every teacher wants banned from every essay, and every child writes it anyway.

grammar[1].subheading: Which past where, and don’t slip into the present
grammar[1].blocks[1].title: Don’t slip into the present
grammar[1].blocks[1].text: The most common mistake in a written story is switching to the present halfway. Check every verb before you finish.
grammar[1].fact: Germany has many thousands of castles, ruins and palaces, and some are for sale at any given moment. They can be cheap. The roof is not. Heritage laws may stop you changing the windows, and the heating bill has ended many a lifelong dream.

document.intro: A real small plate, on a large green knight made of steel, at Burg Vondern in Oberhausen. Three lines, in handwriting type. It has everything: a legend, a castle, an artist, and a passive without the verb.
document.fact: Almost every castle in Germany has a legend, and a ghost. The Ruhr region around Oberhausen, better known for coal, has some of the most unexpected castles of all, Burg Vondern among them.
document.tasks[1].instruction: Write a short story. Keep it in the written past.
document.tasks[1].note: Your own story: only the word schief is fixed.
reading.intro: A letter from Jonas, who has found a new way of not studying. He plays a knight at a medieval festival, for fifty euros a day and all he can eat. This is his report for the student magazine, in the proper written past.
reading.photos[1].caption: Eine Rüstung: dreißig Kilo, und schwer anzuziehen.
reading.fact: Real knights’ armour weighed about 20 to 30 kilos, and contrary to the old story they could get up and even run in it. Medieval festivals are big business in Germany, with craftsmen, bad lutes and much mead.
